answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can govern identity validation through max-flow trust graphs. Peer interactions establish an endorsement ridge that throttles unverified propagation. When an adversary emits a plume of synthetic identities, voting rights unlock at a glacier pace bounded by bottleneck capacities. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of scarce authentic peer relationships per identity. However, this imposes a severe cold-start penalty on newly initialized honest agents.
